title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 361 (Summary procedure for liquidation)

content.overview: Where the company to be wound up under this Chapter has assets of book value not exceeding one crore rupees, and the company falls within the class of companies for which the Official Liquidator may be appointed as liquidator, the Official Liquidator shall employ a summary procedure for the liquidation of such company. The procedure is as prescribed, and the Official Liquidator shall exercise the powers and perform the duties of a liquidator under this Chapter, subject to such modifications as may be prescribed.
content.glance: For companies with book assets ≤ ₹1 crore in the prescribed class, Official Liquidator uses a summary liquidation procedure as prescribed.
content.study: Section 361 provides a streamlined process for smaller estates. examples.title: Small estate
examples.body: A private company with book assets of ₹40 lakh is ordered to be wound up. The Official Liquidator proceeds under the summary procedure of s. 361.

hypotheticals.question: Is the ₹1 crore threshold based on market value?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 361 refers to assets of book value not exceeding one crore rupees.

misconceptions.trap: All Tribunal windings up must follow the full procedure.
misconceptions.correction: Section 361 mandates a summary procedure for qualifying small-asset companies.
